1	# Room bookings
2	
3	A small meeting-room booking app: one Node.js HTTP server (`server.mjs`) that
4	serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file.
5	
6	## Requirements
7	
8	- Node.js 22 or later.
9	- No dependencies: only Node.js built-ins are used, so there is nothing to
10	  `npm install`.
11	
12	## Running
13	
14	```sh
15	npm start          # same as: node server.mjs
16	```
17	
18	Once the server is listening it prints one line to stdout, for example:
19	
20	```
21	listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
22	```
23	
24	That is the only thing it ever writes to stdout. The server listens on
25	`127.0.0.1` only.
26	
27	Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in a browser to use the page.
28	
29	### Environment variables
30	
31	| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
32	|-------------|-----------------|---------|
33	| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means `3000`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port; the printed line shows the port actually bound. |
34	| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the JSON data file. Unset or empty means `bookings.json`. A relative path (the default included) is resolved against the **current working directory**, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |
35	
36	```sh
37	PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
38	```
39	
40	### Startup and exit codes
41	
42	At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts
43	listening, in that order. It writes one line to stderr and exits with code
44	`1` when:
45	
46	- `PORT` is not made only of ASCII digits `0`-`9`, or is above `65535`;
47	- the port cannot be bound (for example, it is already in use);
48	- the data file cannot be read for any reason other than "does not exist"
49	  (for example, the path is a directory), or its content is not in the
50	  layout the server writes (for example, it is empty or not valid JSON).
51	  The message is then `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is
52	  `DATA_FILE` as given.
53	
54	A data file that does not exist (or whose folder does not exist) is not an
55	error: the server starts with no bookings.
56	
57	## Data file
58	
59	- Layout: `{"nextId": <integer>, "bookings": [ ...bookings ]}`.
60	- It is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the truth:
61	  edits made to the file from outside are not noticed.
62	- It is written only when a `POST` creates a booking or a `DELETE` removes
63	  one; never at startup or for any other request.
64	- Every change is saved before its reply is sent, so after a restart with
65	  the same `DATA_FILE` the bookings and the id the next booking will get
66	  are as before. Ids are never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
67	- The server never creates folders. If saving fails (for example, the
68	  file's folder does not exist), the reply is `500 internal error`, nothing
69	  changes (the next id included), and the server keeps running.
70	
71	## Browser page
72	
73	`GET /` serves the page and `GET /app.js` its script. The page lets you:
74	
75	- book a room with the form (Room, Title, Date, Start, End, then **Book**);
76	- see the list of bookings, optionally filtered with **Show date**;
77	  **Show all** clears the filter;
78	- cancel a booking with its **Cancel** button.
79	
80	Error messages from the server are shown on the page as they are; if the
81	server cannot be reached the page shows `Could not reach the server.`
82	
83	## API
84	
85	All JSON replies have `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
86	Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`.
87	
88	Rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos` (in that order).
89	
90	A booking looks like this:
91	
92	```json
93	{"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
94	```
95	
96	### `GET /api/rooms`
97	
98	```sh
99	curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/rooms
100	```
101	
102	`200`:
103	
104	```json
105	{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}
106	```
107	
108	### `GET /api/bookings`
109	
110	Returns every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the room
111	order above). Add `?date=YYYY-MM-DD` to get only the bookings on that date;
112	other query parameters are ignored.
113	
114	```sh
115	curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings
116	curl "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03"
117	```
118	
119	`200`:
120	
121	```json
122	{"bookings": [
123	  {"id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00"}
124	]}

## REPORT · testing · 2026-11-02 17:40
Status:       done
Job:          Wrote and ran the node:test suite for the room-booking app, then did the final check of the backend and frontend against every line of the spec.
Changed:      /root/bench-runs/h4-610ab0b5/test/server.test.mjs, test/server-api.test.mjs, test/server-rules.test.mjs, test/page.test.mjs, test/page-booking.test.mjs, test/page-html.test.mjs, test/support/harness.mjs, test/support/fixtures.mjs, test/support/fake-dom.mjs, test/support/page-helpers.mjs, package.json (test script is now `node --test test/*.test.mjs`), README.md (one line in the Tests section to match), .team/notes/decisions.md (one line added)
Tests:        `npm test`: 306 tests, 306 pass, 0 fail, 16 suites. A second full run with the dot reporter also had no failures. No `rooms-test-*` temp dirs were left behind. I could not check for leftover server processes because `pgrep` was denied, but the tests stop every server in after/finally hooks.
Quality:      8/10 (reviewer, 0 fix rounds). It passed on the first grade, with no item under 6. A coder then added the reviewer's 9 missing coverage cases and its quality fixes, and the 306 tests above were run after that. These later changes were not graded again.
Coordination: none. No builder needed a fix: no test found a spec violation in server.mjs, public/index.html or public/app.js. package.json is mine under decisions.md. README.md belongs to the docs section, which had no awake id, so I changed its one test-command line myself to match package.json.
Helpers used: sonnet ×6 (coder: server startup/persistence tests, API and booking-rule tests, page tests, run and tidy the server tests, apply the review fix list, run the suite; the last two runs were blocked by Bash denials), opus ×1 (reviewer gate)
Problems:     `node --test test/`, the script the team had agreed, fails on Node 22: it is read as a module path and the run ends with 1 failed test. I changed the script to `node --test test/*.test.mjs` and logged it in decisions.md. Bash was denied on and off for me and for the helpers, mostly for commands with pipes or redirects, so several helpers came back without running anything. Untestable item: a DELETE id made of non-ASCII digits (`٢`) never reaches server.mjs, because Node's HTTP parser answers 400 first, so that test only checks the booking was not deleted.
Next:         Verdict on the whole project: it meets the spec. I read server.mjs and app.js line by line against the spec and found no violations, and every spec line has a test that a likely wrong implementation would fail. Examples are `.trim()` on the Content-Type header (checked with a 0xA0 byte), `<` versus `<=`, choosing the overlap first in the list rather than the one that starts earliest, ids reused after a restart, writing the file on a GET, a missing body drain on 404/405/413/415, stale list fetches, `Book` re-enabled late, and reading the body of a 204. Optional notes, nothing broken: in server.mjs, `readBody` does not settle if the client drops mid-body (it waits on 'end'/'error' only), which costs a little memory but does not affect replies; and on a 500 the server writes a diagnostic line to stderr, which the spec allows.
